newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM to sell mine to Cyprus Amax.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM to sell mine to Cyprus Amax.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) said on Thursday it had signed an agreement with U.S.-based Cyprus Amax Minerals Co for it to acquire 80 percent of ZCCM's Kansanshi copper mine.
Kansanshi is the first ZCCM mine to be sold under Zambia's ambitious privatisation of state assets.

"The chairman of ZCCM, Luke Mwananshiku, today signed an agreement providing for Cyprus Amax Minerals Company to eventually acquire an 80 percent interest in ZCCM's Kansanshi copper mine and deposit," a ZCCM statement said.
Kansanshi has a resource base of 24.4 million tonnes of ore at 2.9 percent copper content and has been operated on a limited scale by ZCCM.
Cyprus Amax -- based in Colorado -- is a leading copper and coal producer and is exploring for base and precious metals worldwide.
The ZCCM statement did not put a value to the transaction.
Zambia Privatisation Agency chief Valentine Chitalu told reporters earlier this week that the agency expected to conclude the privatisation of ZCCM by the end of 1998.
ZCCM assets have been split into different packages for privatisation.
The privatisation of ZCCM, which earns around 90 percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings, is seen as crucial to the survival of Zambia's mining industry.
